scenes.voiceover: What happens when a star drops a banned film? Diljit Dosanjh just did it, and chaos ensued!
scenes.image_prompt: Hook - silhouette before cinema screen with BANNED stamp, phone screens glowing

scenes.voiceover: Zero promotion, no trailer, no countdown. Satluj dropped on ZEE5 like a surprise bombshell.
scenes.image_prompt: Stealth release on streaming platform, film appearing suddenly, notification alerts

scenes.voiceover: Jaswant Singh Khalra exposed secret cremations in Punjab. His story? Uncovered by this daring film.
scenes.image_prompt: Documentary style portrait with archival documents, candlelight, records about Khalra

scenes.voiceover: Censors demanded 127 cuts. Filmmakers refused every one, holding firm against three years of delay.
scenes.image_prompt: Giant red 127 number with scissors and red tape, censorship data card

scenes.voiceover: Gone in 48 hours, but gurdwaras stepped up. Communities gather, keeping the story alive.
scenes.image_prompt: Gurdwara interior with projector, community watching, smartphone with share icon

scenes.voiceover: Still streaming for NRIs. From Toronto to Melbourne, ZEE5 delivers Satluj worldwide.
scenes.image_prompt: World map with glowing markers on NYC, London, Toronto, Melbourne, streaming play button

scenes.voiceover: Five years to make this film. For the diaspora, it’s not just a movie; it's a movement.
scenes.image_prompt: Lone spotlight on empty stage, film reel unwinding into light, dramatic closing
